headline: The European Commission confirmed that the attackers who breached it drove Artex, the open-source AI hacking platform, while PHP closed seven critical code-execution flaws and exploit attempts against Java4Shell began.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers now aim AI frameworks at governments: the European Commission says the crew that breached its systems ran Artex, the same open-source platform the FBI flagged last week in both criminal and state-sponsored hands.

The layer underneath every application absorbed the day's damage, with PHP closing 18 flaws, Ruby fixing seven memory-safety bugs, NGINX patching five critical ones, and database engines falling to accounts that cannot read a single application table.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PHP, Ruby, and Databases Ship Code-Execution Fixes

emerging_trends.text: One provider breach keeps buying attackers thousands of downstream victims, as N-able's hosted mail security cloud, Wellington IT's credit union software, and the CreditNirvana debt collection platform each spilled customer records this week.
emerging_trends.topic_title: N-able Mail Cloud and Wellington IT Breaches Spread

topics.title: nginx2root Exploits Go Public as Splunk Patches 140 Bugs
topics.latest_developments: F5 patched five nginx2root vulnerabilities that let remote, unauthenticated attackers run arbitrary code, and proof-of-concept exploits reached the public, with researchers chaining two of the bugs to a Linux kernel flaw to take root; Xint named the set, Rapid7, Wiz, Ikotas Labs, Palo Alto Networks, and Metnir independently found CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, and nobody has reported exploitation in the wild; Broadcom disclosed a VMware vCenter authentication bypass rated 9.8 that hands a network attacker unauthorized access, shipped fixed versions for every supported branch, and listed no workaround; Splunk fixed nearly 140 flaws across three core products, among them authentication bypass, remote code execution, and privilege escalation; and SonicWall told customers in a Wednesday advisory to replace every Gen 6 and Gen 6.5 appliance and pull it off the internet edge, because SonicOS 6.x now receives no firmware or security updates regardless of severity.
topics.summary: The nginx2root bugs have sat in NGINX's open-source HTTP/2 code since version 1.9.5 shipped on September 22, 2015, and F5 fixed them in 1.31.9 and 1.30.7. Any internet-facing NGINX with HTTP/2 enabled, vCenter console, Splunk deployment, or SonicWall Gen 6 firewall needs action this week.

topics.title: Cisco Expressway and Apache Axis Enter Active Exploitation
topics.latest_developments: Attackers exploited a Cisco Expressway vulnerability soon after a proof of concept went out, hacking clustered Expressway devices at a Russian organization and staging tooling for lateral movement; the Apache Software Foundation warned of attacks on Roller through CVE-2026-129448, the unauthenticated XML-RPC deserialization bug rated 9.8, while a separate Apache Axis flaw now serves as the way into Confluence Data Center; CISA tied its four newest Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entries, covering Synology DiskStation Manager, BerriAI LiteLLM, Apache Axis, and Vanderbilt University's Research Electronic Data Capture platform, to ransomware, cryptomining, and LLMjacking, and ordered federal civilian agencies to fix the Perforce Puppet Enterprise flaw CVE-2026-115731; Drupal patched a critical remote code execution bug that lets an attacker without credentials drive the built-in installer into reinstalling a site, and told site owners to expect exploits fast.
topics.summary: Five widely deployed products—Cisco Expressway, Apache Roller, Apache Axis, Puppet Enterprise, and Drupal—now carry unauthenticated paths to code execution with attacks already running. Patch the internet-facing ones first and treat the Puppet server as a route to every endpoint it configures.

topics.title: PHP, Ruby, and Databases Ship Code-Execution Fixes
topics.latest_developments: PHP shipped its releases on November 19, 2026, closing 18 vulnerabilities, seven of them critical remote code execution bugs, among them CVE-2026-115560 in session upload progress and phpAfterShell, CVE-2026-126714, which cuts a session write off at the right moment so file-based session storage returns objects the attacker chose and a gadget chain in the application turns them into commands; PHP 8.6 landed the same day, starting sessions with session.use_strict_mode and session.cookie_httponly on and session.cookie_samesite set to Lax; Ruby fixed seven memory-safety bugs in its regular expression engine and string case-conversion code, and its maintainers say proof-of-concept exploits run code through five of them; and a researcher published working exploits that carry a low-privilege database account into code execution on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and ClickHouse servers, plus a separate Oracle chain.
topics.summary: Three of the most widely deployed back-end runtimes now carry fresh unauthenticated or low-privilege paths to the operating system account under the service. Upgrade PHP and Ruby today, and audit which database accounts can create objects or call engine functions.

sources.title: PHP Patches Seven Critical RCE Vulnerabilities

Ruby Releases Fixes for 7 Regex and String Flaws, Warns 5 Have Proof-of-Concept RCE

topics.title: AI Agents Run on Their Builders' Credentials
topics.latest_developments: Nudge Security, drawing on telemetry from its customers' environments, found that the AI agents employees assemble inside project trackers, CRMs, and automation tools run on the credentials of whoever built them and inherit that person's access to company data, with no one monitoring how the agents spend it; Wired documented Artex, the open-source AI penetration-testing framework, as the point-and-shoot tool newcomers now use to scan and attack targets through chatbot prompts; Google built a replica of the internet, a sandbox its Chrome team calls a mirror dimension, to train browsing agents without turning them loose on real sites; Microsoft moved its Perception agentic security platform out of preview, making four blue team agents and the Recon Agent generally available; and Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute, which post-trains and runs open-weight models, for $4.5 billion in stock.
topics.summary: Employee-built agents carry human entitlements into automated workflows while attackers drive the same agent frameworks offensively. Inventory which agents run in your environment, whose identity each one uses, and what systems it can reach.

topics.title: N-able Mail Cloud and Wellington IT Breaches Spread
topics.latest_developments: Transport for London told roughly 265,000 Oyster photocard customers that intruders may have taken their account details; NVIDIA said it has found no indication that anyone compromised its systems after the Gentlemen ransomware crew listed the chipmaker on its dark web leak site; N-able disclosed on Wednesday, November 18, 2026 that unknown attackers reached a server in its Mail Assure and Spam Experts Hosted Cloud, and the company disabled management interfaces and APIs across three regions while its investigation continues; a reported attack on Wellington IT exposed sensitive member information at 50 credit unions, most of them in Ireland; and Wired reported that two vulnerabilities in CreditNirvana, the AI debt collection platform, left 6.6 million accounts and 315,000 call recordings open, along with emails, texts, and credit reports.
topics.summary: Five victims this week sit downstream of a provider or a transit operator: a hosted email security cloud, a credit union software vendor, a ransomware leak-site listing, a debt collection platform holding financial records, and London's fare card system. Customers of each should force credential rotation and review what access the provider holds.

topics.title: Washington Targets Scam Payments and a Palantir Spy
topics.latest_developments: The Department of Justice joined the Department of Homeland Security on the Threat Disruption Center, which opened inside the Homeland Security Task Force's National Coordination Center in Fairfax, Virginia, giving investigators shared tooling to sort victim complaints, map the criminal groups behind them, open a direct channel to private companies that work with victims, and stop payments before the money leaves for foreign scam, cybercrime, and sextortion networks; Coinbase blocked $4.7 million in cryptocurrency transfers to a fake giveaway that ran an AI-generated deepfake of Elon Musk during a Tesla livestream more than 500,000 people watched; federal prosecutors charged Igor Andreevich D'iu, a Russian national recruited through Telegram, with acting as a Moscow agent in a surveillance campaign against employees of a defense technology company The Record understands to be Palantir Technologies; and a federal bankruptcy judge cleared Google to take the data of the defunct Spirit Airlines for $10 million, with protections attached, for use in AI projects.
topics.summary: The United States is attacking fraud at the payment layer while prosecuting human-intelligence collection against defense contractor staff. Finance and insider-threat teams gain a new federal contact point for both.

topics.title: Java4Shell Draws Live Exploit Attempts
topics.latest_developments: GreyNoise, watchTowr, and Cloudflare each reported probing and exploit attempts against CVE-2026-114938, and Cisco, Elastic, Red Hat, and Siemens published advisories spelling out which of their products carry the vulnerable runtime; Dark Reading reported that researchers found the flaw using AI.
topics.summary: Java4Shell is a memory corruption bug in the Base64 decoder of the x86-64 HotSpot Java Virtual Machine that hands an attacker who never logs in remote code execution on Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak. Any host running Java 17.0.6 or later on an Intel or AMD processor with AVX-512 VBMI needs the patch now.

topics.title: Ukraine Arrests a Fake IT Support Ransomware Crew
topics.latest_developments: Ukraine's National Police described how the four suspects worked: they studied each target, then telephoned employees posing as IT support staff to talk their way into corporate networks, and the case ran more than two years with the FBI; The Record identified oil and healthcare companies in the United States among the 28 victims that paid more than $40.5 million.
topics.summary: Ukrainian authorities detained four members of an international ransomware operation that opened its intrusions with voice phishing rather than malware. Help desks and their callers need verification steps that survive a convincing phone call.

topics.title: ICE Pays AT&T to Mine Call Records
topics.latest_developments: An internal Immigration and Customs Enforcement document that 404 Media obtained shows the agency paying AT&T for raw data and analytical services under the Hemisphere program, and privacy experts and members of Congress call the arrangement a mass surveillance effort that may touch trillions of phone records; separately, a British tribunal confirmed that the government served Apple with a secret legal notice targeting the cryptographic protections on iCloud accounts, ending almost two years in which officials refused to acknowledge the order.
topics.summary: Hemisphere gives federal investigators searchable access to AT&T call detail records, including calls that merely cross AT&T's network, and the British notice puts iCloud's encryption under a demand Apple cannot discuss. Anyone whose threat model includes United States or British legal demands should assume telephone metadata sits inside a commercial analytics service and treat cloud backup encryption as contested.

sources.title: ICE Is Paying AT&T to Dig Through a Mountain of Call Records

topics.title: European Commission Breached With Artex
topics.latest_developments: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack on its systems and said the intruders used an AI tool; POLITICO reported that CERT-EU, the computer emergency response team for the European Union institutions, identified that tool as Artex, the open-source AI hacking platform the FBI warned about last week in the hands of both criminals and state-sponsored groups.
topics.summary: Artex chains reconnaissance, exploitation, and follow-on steps from a short prompt, which has carried some intrusions from first contact to privileged access in under three hours. Defenders should tune detection for machine-speed scanning and exploit chaining, and shorten the window between a vendor patch and their own.

sources.title: European Commission confirms cyberattack, says hackers used AI tool

business_politics.title: The Dollar Reaches a 19-Month High
business_politics.latest_developments: The DXY dollar index touched 103.974 overnight into Thursday, November 19, its highest level in 19 months, before easing back during the New York session.
business_politics.summary: Danske Bank strategist Antti Ilvonen told the Wall Street Journal the rally has further to run because the Federal Reserve looks likely to raise rates more than the European Central Bank, the Bank of England, or the Bank of Japan. A dollar at these levels squeezes Asian currencies and every borrower funded in dollars, and it follows Governor Christopher Waller's call for an outsized December increase.

sources.title: Dollar Has Further Scope to Rally as Fed Could Out-Hike Peers

business_politics.title: Germany Puts Its Cyber Threat Level at Critical
business_politics.latest_developments: A ransomware group leaked data belonging to thousands of Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase customers Thursday, November 19, with payment services still running and the theft unconnected to this week's banking outages, hours after Germany's security authorities reported an artificial-intelligence-driven surge in hacking attempts and rated the national threat level critical.
business_politics.summary: New artificial-intelligence tools let attackers find and exploit software flaws far faster, and the German assessment lands a week after outages knocked out systems at Microsoft, JPMorgan Chase, and other large companies. The Economist traces those American failures to frenzied patching and cyber-attack preparation that manufacture fragility of their own, which puts operational risk at banks and cloud providers in the same frame as the attackers.

business_politics.title: Anthropic Debuts on the Nasdaq
business_politics.latest_developments: Anthropic shares began trading midday Thursday, November 19, and soared from the $83 offering price, and the broader market turned down after the open, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average leading stocks lower.
business_politics.summary: Anthropic, the San Francisco maker of the Claude chatbot, raised $81.3 billion in the largest initial public offering on record and becomes the first artificial-intelligence lab to trade publicly, with a majority of its more than 5,000 employees in line to become millionaires. The company's layered funding structure leaves analysts arguing over whether the business is worth $1.1 trillion or $2 trillion, and the opening prints give investors their clearest read on appetite for the AI build-out after weeks of selling in Nvidia and data-center shares.

business_politics.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Hold the First Trilateral Summit
business_politics.latest_developments: The three leaders closed the Shenzhen summit Thursday, November 19, with a joint denunciation of nuclear war and a show of unity on energy security, they reached no major breakthrough, and Vladimir Putin then invited European leaders to Moscow while holding to his hardline terms for ending the war in Ukraine.
business_politics.summary: Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin met in the southern Chinese city during the week of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum, the first meeting ever to put the American, Chinese, and Russian heads of state at one table, and Trump told the room, "We are really making history." Germany hosted 40 delegations in Berlin the same day to back Kyiv and blunt the summit's Yalta 2.0 optics, and the Wall Street Journal argues Trump's leverage abroad is contracting even as he convenes the meeting.

business_politics.latest_developments: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Samsung Electronics suspended some chip shipments to Chinese customers, the Financial Times reported Thursday, November 19, days after the Commerce Department imposed its new export controls.
business_politics.summary: The two largest contract chipmakers supply processors that go into Chinese phones, servers, and cars, so a sustained halt starves Chinese technology firms of advanced silicon. Alibaba, which reported a sharp earnings rebound Thursday on improving artificial-intelligence profitability, named tighter scrutiny of chip exports to China as a fresh risk to that growth engine.

business.latest_developments: TribLive reported Thursday, November 19, that a developer signed a $3.7 million option on more than 41 acres in Westmoreland Industrial Park North to build a large warehouse and industrial facility in East Huntingdon Township.
business.summary: The site sits in the Westmoreland County industrial park off the Route 119 corridor, where the county has courted warehouse and light manufacturing tenants for years. An option gives the developer time to line up permits and tenants before buying the ground outright.

business.title: Viatris Closes Its $1.65 Billion Pacira Deal
business.latest_developments: Viatris completed its acquisition of Pacira BioSciences in a deal valued at $1.65 billion, the company announced Tuesday, November 17, and WPXI reported Thursday, November 19.
business.summary: Viatris, the Canonsburg drugmaker formed in 2020 from Mylan and the Upjohn business of Pfizer, ranks among the largest public companies based in Western Pennsylvania. Pacira develops pain medications, and the purchase pushes Viatris further beyond generics into branded treatment.

business.summary: Achieva runs a $57 million operation providing services, family supports, employment programs, and advocacy for people with disabilities across the Pittsburgh region. Hower inherits one of the larger human-services employers in Allegheny County.

business.title: U.S. Steel and the Steelworkers Reach a Tentative Contract
business.latest_developments: The United Steelworkers announced a tentative agreement with U.S. Steel Thursday morning, November 19, covering more than 10,000 workers at 13 facilities.
business.summary: The proposed deal commits $4.5 billion in capital investment at union-represented sites of U.S. Steel, the Pittsburgh company Nippon Steel acquired in 2025, and the Pittsburgh-based United Steelworkers negotiated it for mills that anchor employment across Western Pennsylvania. The capital pledge determines which plants get modernized and which workers keep their jobs.

business.title: AAA Sees Thanksgiving Travel Slip
business.latest_developments: AAA forecast that fewer people will drive or fly for Thanksgiving this year, WTAE reported Thursday, November 19, the first decline in three years, while cruise, bus, and train bookings climb.
business.summary: The forecast covers the holiday week leading to Thanksgiving on Thursday, November 26, 2026, and sets the volume expectations for Pittsburgh International Airport, the Pennsylvania Turnpike, and Amtrak service through the region. Airlines and hotels price the holiday off these projections, and the shift toward rail and bus travel follows a month of airline disruption.

sources.title: Thanksgiving travel dips for the first time in three years

around_town.title: An Arbitration Panel Gives Pittsburgh Police 19%
around_town.latest_developments: An arbitration panel signed a four-year contract Thursday, November 19, that raises pay for Pittsburgh's rank-and-file police officers by a total of 19%, and the officers' union announced the award.
around_town.summary: The bureau's officers had worked for months without a settled contract, and the award sets the city's largest public safety payroll through the end of the decade. The cost lands as City Council works through Mayor Corey O'Connor's 2027 budget.

around_town.summary: Light Up Night fills the Golden Triangle Saturday, November 21, and the street closings reroute buses that normally run through Market Square, Liberty Avenue, and the surrounding blocks. Riders heading downtown that evening should expect moved stops.

around_town.summary: The Allegheny County borough sits south of Pittsburgh along Route 51, and the repeat failure on the same residential street points to aging pipe under the neighborhood. Crews worked the site through the morning.

around_town.title: Sto-Rox Teachers Authorize a Strike
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE reported Thursday, November 19, that the Sto-Rox Education Association has now worked 142 days under an expired contract, a day after members voted with full support to authorize a strike, and union officials said they will hold off on a walkout for now.
around_town.summary: The Sto-Rox School District, which serves McKees Rocks and Stowe Township in Allegheny County, has yet to settle terms with its teachers, and the union had not taken a strike authorization vote in decades. The vote hands union leadership the power to call a walkout whenever it judges one necessary, which would idle classes for the district's students.

around_town.summary: The agreement would let Charleroi Regional Police officers act as federal immigration enforcement agents in the Washington County borough, where the Haitian population has thinned since federal Temporary Protected Status ended. team_usa.title: Arena Blasts the U.S. Coaching Search
team_usa.latest_developments: Bruce Arena said U.S. Soccer does not "have a clue" how to replace Mauricio Pochettino, ESPN reported Thursday, November 19, and the network argued the same day that the change opens the midfield to fringe players who fell out of Pochettino's plans.
team_usa.summary: Arena, who coached the United States men's national team at the 2002 and 2006 World Cups and now manages the San Jose Earthquakes, took aim at the federation two days after Pochettino left for Manchester United. Steve Cherundolo runs the December camp on an interim basis while U.S. Soccer, with women's coach Emma Hayes helping assess candidates, searches for a permanent hire ahead of the 2030 cycle.

team_usa.title: Sanchez Wins the NWSL MVP Award
team_usa.latest_developments: The National Women's Soccer League named Ashley Sanchez its 2026 Most Valuable Player Wednesday, November 18, placing her ahead of Trinity Rodman in the voting.
team_usa.summary: Sanchez, the North Carolina Courage forward and a United States international, tied the league record with 20 goals this season. The award caps a year that puts her in the conversation for Emma Hayes's World Cup qualifying squads.

team_usa.title: The NWSL Final Arrives With Old Problems
team_usa.latest_developments: ESPN reported Thursday, November 19, that record revenue has failed to solve the National Women's Soccer League's stadium and scheduling problems as the Kansas City Current and the Washington Spirit prepare to meet in Saturday's championship, November 21.
team_usa.summary: Venue conflicts pushed both semifinals into unsuitable buildings last weekend, and Gotham FC forward Midge Purce called the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium assignment inexcusable. The final pairs Kansas City against a Washington side chasing its third straight title with Trinity Rodman leading the attack.
